column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|05-27|1923|Χένρι Κίσινγκερ|Henry Kissinger|Henry Kissinger was born in Germany and left with his family for the United States in 1938. He was national security adviser and secretary of state under Nixon and Ford. In 1973 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for the negotiations on Vietnam, an award that provoked controversy.

bio|05-27|1964|Τζαβαχαρλάλ Νεχρού|Jawaharlal Nehru|Jawaharlal Nehru was a leading member of the movement for India's independence and the first prime minister of the country, from 1947 until his death. He worked with Gandhi and was the father of Indira Gandhi.

bio|05-28|1759|Ουίλιαμ Πιτ ο νεότερος|William Pitt the Younger|William Pitt the Younger became prime minister of Britain in 1783, at the age of 24, the youngest in the country's history. He led the war against revolutionary France and against Napoleon. He died in 1806.

bio|05-28|1849|Αν Μπροντέ|Anne Brontë|Anne Brontë was an English writer, the youngest of the Brontë sisters. She wrote the novels "Agnes Grey" and "The Tenant of Wildfell Hall". She died young, of tuberculosis, at the age of 29.

bio|05-28|1908|Ίαν Φλέμινγκ|Ian Fleming|Ian Fleming was a British writer and an officer of the Navy's secret intelligence service. He created the spy James Bond and a series of novels beginning with "Casino Royale" in 1953.

bio|05-28|1912|Πάτρικ Γουάιτ|Patrick White|Patrick White was an Australian writer. He wrote novels such as "Aunt Rhoda" and "The Man with the Jeep". In 1973 he became the first Australian to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|05-28|1937|Άλφρεντ Άντλερ|Alfred Adler|Alfred Adler died in 1937 in Aberdeen, Scotland, on a lecture tour. He was an Austrian psychologist and the founder of individual psychology, known for the concept of the "inferiority complex".

bio|05-28|1968|Κάιλι Μινόγκ|Kylie Minogue|Kylie Minogue is an Australian singer and actress. She became known through the series "Neighbours" and with hits such as "The Loco-Motion", "Can't Get You Out of My Head" and "Spinning Around".
bio|05-28|1971|Μάρκο Ρούμπιο|Marco Rubio|Marco Rubio is an American Republican politician of Cuban descent. He was a senator for Florida, and from 2025 he has been United States Secretary of State.

bio|05-28|1972|Εδουάρδος Η΄|Edward VIII|Edward VIII became king of the United Kingdom in 1936 and abdicated after a few months in order to marry the American Wallis Simpson. He became Duke of Windsor and lived in France. He died in 1972.

bio|05-28|2014|Μάγια Αγγέλου|Maya Angelou|Maya Angelou died in 2014. She was an American poet and writer, and she wrote the autobiography "I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings". She was also an activist for civil rights.

bio|05-29|1489|Μιμάρ Σινάν|Mimar Sinan|Mimar Sinan was the greatest architect of the Ottoman Empire. He was court architect for many years and designed more than 300 buildings, such as the Süleymaniye Mosque in Istanbul and the Selimiye in Edirne.

bio|05-29|1500|Βαρθολομαίος Ντιάζ|Bartolomeu Dias|Bartolomeu Dias was a Portuguese explorer. In 1488 he became the first European to reach the southernmost tip of Africa, the Cape of Good Hope. He died in 1500 in a shipwreck.

bio|05-29|1630|Κάρολος Β΄|Charles II|Charles II was king of England, Scotland and Ireland from 1660, when the monarchy was restored after the regime of Cromwell. He was a patron of the arts and the sciences.

bio|05-29|1914|Τένσινγκ Νοργκέι|Tenzing Norgay|Tenzing Norgay was a Sherpa and mountaineer. On 29 May 1953, together with Edmund Hillary, he became one of the first people to reach the summit of Mount Everest.

bio|05-29|1917|Τζον Φ. Κένεντι|John F. Kennedy|John Fitzgerald Kennedy was the 35th president of the United States, from 1961. He was the youngest person elected to the office and the first Catholic. He faced the Cuban Missile Crisis and launched the Apollo programme. He was assassinated in 1963 in Dallas.

bio|05-29|1929|Πίτερ Χιγκς|Peter Higgs|Peter Higgs was a British theoretical physicist. In 1964 he proposed that there is a particle, the Higgs boson, that gives mass to other particles. Its discovery in 2012 led to the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2013.

bio|05-29|1958|Χουάν Ραμόν Χιμένεθ|Juan Ramón Jiménez|Juan Ramón Jiménez was a Spanish poet. He wrote the prose poem "Platero and I", about a donkey. In 1956 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|05-29|1979|Μαίρη Πίκφορντ|Mary Pickford|Mary Pickford died in 1979. She was a Canadian actress and producer of the silent cinema, and together with Chaplin and others she founded the United Artists company. She won an Oscar in 1930.

bio|05-29|1994|Έριχ Χόνεκερ|Erich Honecker|Erich Honecker was the leader of East Germany from 1971 to 1989. He was responsible for the construction of the Berlin Wall. After the fall of the regime he took refuge in Chile, where he died in 1994.

bio|05-30|1431|Ιωάννα της Λωραίνης|Joan of Arc|Joan of Arc, known as Jeanne d'Arc, was a French peasant woman who led the French to lift the siege of Orléans. She was captured by the Burgundians, who handed her over to the English, and she was burned at the stake in Rouen in 1431. She was canonised in 1920.

bio|05-30|1640|Πέτερ Πάουλ Ρούμπενς|Peter Paul Rubens|Peter Paul Rubens was a Flemish Baroque painter. He painted large works with mythological and religious themes, with dynamic movement and fleshy figures. He was also a diplomat.

bio|05-30|1778|Βολταίρος|Voltaire|Voltaire, real name François-Marie Arouet, was a French writer and philosopher of the Enlightenment. He wrote "Candide" and the "Philosophical Letters". He defended tolerance and freedom of thought.

bio|05-30|1814|Μιχαήλ Μπακούνιν|Mikhail Bakunin|Mikhail Bakunin was a Russian revolutionary and theorist of anarchism. He took part in uprisings in Europe, was exiled to Siberia and escaped. He clashed with Marx in the First International.

bio|05-30|1908|Χάνες Αλφβέν|Hannes Alfvén|Hannes Alfvén was a Swedish physicist. He developed magnetohydrodynamics, and in 1970 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for his study of electromagnetic phenomena in plasmas.

bio|05-30|1909|Μπένι Γκούντμαν|Benny Goodman|Benny Goodman was an American clarinettist and jazz bandleader. He was called the "King of Swing", and he led some of the first big bands with black and white musicians playing together.
bio|05-30|1934|Αλεξέι Λεόνοφ|Alexei Leonov|Alexei Leonov was a Soviet cosmonaut. On 18 March 1965 he became the first person to leave a spacecraft to walk in space. He was also a painter.

bio|05-30|1960|Μπορίς Παστερνάκ|Boris Pasternak|Boris Pasternak died in 1960. He was a Russian poet and the author of "Doctor Zhivago", which was banned in the Soviet Union. He had been forced to decline the Nobel Prize of 1958.

bio|05-30|1980|Στίβεν Τζέραρντ|Steven Gerrard|Steven Gerrard is an English former footballer. He played as a midfielder for Liverpool and was captain of the team that won the Champions League in 2005. He later became a coach.

bio|05-31|1594|Τιντορέττο|Tintoretto|Tintoretto, real name Jacopo Robusti, was an Italian painter from Venice. He became known for his dynamic paintings with strong contrasts of light, such as "The Last Supper". He was one of the leading painters of the late Renaissance.

bio|05-31|1809|Γιόζεφ Χάυντν|Joseph Haydn|Joseph Haydn died in Vienna in 1809. He was an Austrian composer of the Classical period, with more than 100 symphonies, and is regarded as the "father of the symphony". He was a friend of Mozart and the teacher of Beethoven.

bio|05-31|1819|Γουόλτ Γουίτμαν|Walt Whitman|Walt Whitman was born on Long Island, New York. He was an American poet and journalist and wrote the collection "Leaves of Grass", in free verse, with hymns to democracy and to the human body.

bio|05-31|1832|Εβαρίστ Γκαλουά|Évariste Galois|Évariste Galois was a French mathematician. He founded group theory, also called Galois theory, on the solutions of polynomial equations. He was killed in a duel in 1832, at the age of 20.

bio|05-31|1887|Σαιν-Τζον Περς|Saint-John Perse|Saint-John Perse, real name Alexis Leger, was a French diplomat and poet. He wrote "Anabasis" and other works in an epic style. In 1960 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|05-31|1930|Κλιντ Ίστγουντ|Clint Eastwood|Clint Eastwood is an American actor and director. He became known through the Westerns of Sergio Leone and the role of "Dirty Harry". He won Oscars for Best Director for "Unforgiven" and "Million Dollar Baby".

bio|05-31|1962|Άντολφ Άιχμαν|Adolf Eichmann|Adolf Eichmann was executed in Israel on 31 May 1962. He was an SS officer and one of the organisers of the extermination of the Jews. He had fled to Argentina and was abducted by Israel in 1960.

bio|05-31|1963|Βίκτορ Όρμπαν|Viktor Orbán|Viktor Orbán is a Hungarian politician of the Fidesz party. He was prime minister of Hungary from 1998 to 2002 and again from 2010. His policy, which he calls "illiberal democracy", causes disputes within the European Union.

bio|05-31|1989|Μάρκο Ρόις|Marco Reus|Marco Reus is a German footballer. He has played for Borussia Dortmund and the German national team. He suffered from many injuries and did not take part in the 2014 World Cup, which Germany won.

bio|06-01|1616|Τοκουγκάβα Ιεγιάσου|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Tokugawa Ieyasu was a Japanese warlord. He founded the Tokugawa shogunate and governed from 1603, after his victory at the Battle of Sekigahara. The shogunate lasted about 265 years.

bio|06-01|1804|Μιχαήλ Γκλίνκα|Mikhail Glinka|Mikhail Glinka was a Russian composer. He is regarded as the founder of the Russian national school of music and wrote the operas "A Life for the Tsar" and "Ruslan and Lyudmila".

bio|06-01|1868|Τζέιμς Μπιουκάναν|James Buchanan|James Buchanan, the 15th president of the United States from 1857 to 1861, died in 1868. His presidency took place in the period of tension that led to the American Civil War.

bio|06-01|1926|Μέριλιν Μονρόε|Marilyn Monroe|Marilyn Monroe, real name Norma Jean Mortenson, was an American actress and a sex symbol. She appeared in "Some Like It Hot" and "Gentlemen Prefer Blondes". She died in 1962, at the age of 36.

bio|06-01|1937|Μόργκαν Φρίμαν|Morgan Freeman|Morgan Freeman is an American actor. He won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for "Million Dollar Baby" and appeared in "The Shawshank Redemption" and "Se7en". His voice is very recognisable.
bio|06-01|1952|Τζον Ντιούι|John Dewey|John Dewey was an American philosopher and educator. He was one of the founders of pragmatism and supported education based on experience and on democracy.

bio|06-01|1961|Νταϊάνα Σπένσερ|Diana, Princess of Wales|Diana Spencer was a British aristocrat who married Prince Charles in 1981 and became Princess of Wales. She was known for her charitable work. She was killed in a road accident in Paris in 1997.

bio|06-01|1968|Έλεν Κέλερ|Helen Keller|Helen Keller was an American writer and activist. She became blind and deaf in infancy, but with the help of her teacher, Annie Sullivan, she learned to communicate and graduated from university.
bio|06-01|1975|Νικόλ Πασινιάν|Nikol Pashinyan|Nikol Pashinyan is an Armenian politician and journalist. He led the "Velvet Revolution" of 2018 and became prime minister of Armenia.

bio|06-02|1701|Μαντλέν ντε Σκυντερύ|Madeleine de Scudéry|Madeleine de Scudéry was a French writer. She was known for her lengthy novels "Artamène, or The Great Cyrus" and "Clélie", and for her salon in Paris.

bio|06-02|1740|Μαρκήσιος ντε Σαντ|Marquis de Sade|The Marquis de Sade was a French aristocrat and writer. His works deal with harsh and immoral themes, and he was imprisoned for much of his life. The term "sadism" comes from his name.

bio|06-02|1840|Τόμας Χάρντι|Thomas Hardy|Thomas Hardy was born in Dorset, England. He was a writer and poet and wrote the novels "Tess of the d'Urbervilles" and "Jude the Obscure". In his last years he wrote mainly poetry.

bio|06-02|1857|Έντουαρντ Έλγκαρ|Edward Elgar|Edward Elgar was an English composer. He wrote the "Enigma Variations", a cello concerto and "Pomp and Circumstance", of which "Land of Hope and Glory" became an unofficial national anthem.

bio|06-02|1876|Χρίστο Μπότεφ|Hristo Botev|Hristo Botev was a Bulgarian poet and revolutionary. He led the April Uprising against the Ottomans in 1876 and was killed during the fighting. He is regarded as a national hero of Bulgaria.

bio|06-02|1882|Τζουζέπε Γκαριμπάλντι|Giuseppe Garibaldi|Giuseppe Garibaldi was an Italian general and national hero. He led the Expedition of the Thousand in 1860, which took Sicily and Naples and contributed to the unification of Italy. He also helped the Greek cause.

bio|06-02|1940|Κωνσταντίνος Β΄|Constantine II|Constantine II was the last king of the Greeks, from 1964 to 1973. He was an Olympic sailing champion in 1960. After the coup of 21 April 1967 he resisted the junta unsuccessfully and went abroad. The monarchy was abolished by referendum in 1974.

bio|06-02|1988|Σέρχιο Αγουέρο|Sergio Agüero|Sergio Agüero is a former Argentine footballer. He played for Manchester City and scored the goal that brought the club the league title in 2012, in the last minute. He is the club's all-time top scorer.
bio|06-02|1990|Ρεξ Χάρισον|Rex Harrison|Rex Harrison was an English actor. He won the Academy Award for Best Actor for "My Fair Lady", in the role of Professor Higgins.
bio|06-03|1865|Γεώργιος Ε΄|George V|George V was king of the United Kingdom from 1910 to 1936. He reigned during the First World War, and in 1917 he changed the name of the royal house to Windsor.

bio|06-03|1875|Ζωρζ Μπιζέ|Georges Bizet|Georges Bizet was a French composer. He wrote the opera "Carmen", which was not successful at its premiere in 1875 and became famous after his death. He died at the age of 36, a few months later.

bio|06-03|1924|Φραντς Κάφκα|Franz Kafka|Franz Kafka was a Czech Jewish writer who wrote in German. He wrote "The Metamorphosis", "The Trial" and "The Castle". He died of tuberculosis in 1924, and most of his works were published after his death.

bio|06-03|1926|Άλλεν Γκίνσμπεργκ|Allen Ginsberg|Allen Ginsberg was an American poet and a pioneer of the Beat Generation. He became known with the poem "Howl" of 1956, which led to an obscenity trial. He was an activist for gay rights and against war.

bio|06-03|1931|Ραούλ Κάστρο|Raúl Castro|Raúl Castro is a Cuban politician and the brother of Fidel Castro. He took part in the Cuban Revolution, was minister of defence, and from 2008 to 2018 was president of Cuba. He resigned from the leadership of the Communist Party in 2021.

bio|06-03|1986|Ραφαέλ Ναδάλ|Rafael Nadal|Rafael Nadal is a Spanish tennis player. He has won 22 Grand Slam tournaments, 14 of them at Roland Garros, and an Olympic gold medal in 2008. He has been called "the King of Clay".

bio|06-03|1989|Ρουχολάχ Χομεϊνί|Ruhollah Khomeini|Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini was an Iranian religious leader. He led the Islamic Revolution of 1979, which overthrew the Shah, and was Supreme Leader of Iran until his death in 1989.

bio|06-03|2016|Μοχάμεντ Άλι|Muhammad Ali|Muhammad Ali died in 2016. He was an American boxer and three-time heavyweight world champion. He became known for his rhetoric and for his opposition to the war in Vietnam.

bio|06-04|1738|Γεώργιος Γ΄|George III|George III was king of Great Britain and Ireland from 1760. During his reign the United States gained independence and the Napoleonic Wars took place. In his later years he suffered from mental illness.

bio|06-04|1798|Τζάκομο Καζανόβα|Giacomo Casanova|Giacomo Casanova died in 1798 in Bohemia. He was an Italian writer and adventurer from Venice, and he described his adventures in his memoirs, "The Story of My Life".

bio|06-04|1867|Καρλ Γκούσταφ Έμιλ Μάνερχαϊμ|Carl Gustaf Emil Mannerheim|Carl Gustaf Emil Mannerheim was a Finnish soldier and politician. He led the White Army in the Finnish Civil War of 1918, was commander-in-chief in the Second World War and was president of Finland in 1944 to 1946.

bio|06-04|1876|Αμπντούλ Αζίζ|Abdulaziz|Abdulaziz was Ottoman sultan from 1861 to 1876. He visited Europe, something no sultan had done before, and modernised the fleet. He was deposed in 1876 and died a few days later.

bio|06-04|1941|Γουλιέλμος Β΄|Wilhelm II|Wilhelm II was the last German emperor and king of Prussia, from 1888 to 1918. He abdicated at the end of the First World War and lived in the Netherlands, where he died in 1941.

bio|06-04|1942|Ράινχαρντ Χάιντριχ|Reinhard Heydrich|Reinhard Heydrich was a senior SS official and one of the main organisers of the Holocaust. He was mortally wounded in 1942 in Prague in an attack by Czech resistance fighters, and he died on 4 June.
bio|06-04|1952|Μπρονίσλαφ Κομορόφσκι|Bronisław Komorowski|Bronisław Komorowski is a Polish politician. He was president of Poland from 2010 to 2015, after the death of Lech Kaczyński in an air crash.

bio|06-04|1975|Αντζελίνα Τζολί|Angelina Jolie|Angelina Jolie is an American actress, director and humanitarian. She won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for "Girl, Interrupted". She is a special envoy of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees.
bio|06-04|1985|Λούκας Ποντόλσκι|Lukas Podolski|Lukas Podolski is a German footballer of Polish origin. He played for Cologne, Bayern Munich and Arsenal, and he won the 2014 World Cup with Germany.

bio|06-05|1599|Ντιέγο Βελάθκεθ|Diego Velázquez|Diego Velázquez was a Spanish painter of the Golden Age. He was court painter to Philip IV and painted "Las Meninas" and the portrait of Pope Innocent X.

bio|06-05|1826|Καρλ Μαρία φον Βέμπερ|Carl Maria von Weber|Carl Maria von Weber was a German composer of the Romantic era. He wrote the opera "Der Freischütz", which was the first great German Romantic opera. He died in London in 1826.

bio|06-05|1883|Τζων Μέυναρντ Κέυνς|John Maynard Keynes|John Maynard Keynes was a British economist. In his work "The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money" he argued that the state must intervene to deal with recession.

bio|06-05|1898|Φεδερίκο Γκαρθία Λόρκα|Federico García Lorca|Federico García Lorca was a Spanish poet and playwright. He wrote "Blood Wedding", "Yerma" and "The House of Bernarda Alba". He was executed in 1936, at the start of the Spanish Civil War.

bio|06-05|1900|Ντένις Γκέιμπορ|Dennis Gabor|Dennis Gabor was born in Budapest and lived in Britain. He was an engineer and physicist and invented holography. In 1971 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|06-05|1971|Μαρκ Γουόλμπεργκ|Mark Wahlberg|Mark Wahlberg is an American actor and producer. He began as a singer under the name Marky Mark, and then became an actor in films such as "The Departed" and "The Fighter".

bio|06-05|1971|Γκέοργκ Λούκατς|Georg Lukács|Georg Lukács was a Hungarian Marxist philosopher and literary critic. He wrote "History and Class Consciousness" and "The Theory of the Novel". He was one of the most important Marxist thinkers of the 20th century.

bio|06-05|2004|Ρόναλντ Ρήγκαν|Ronald Reagan|Ronald Reagan died in 2004. He was the 40th president of the United States, from 1981 to 1989, and a former actor and governor of California. He became known for his tax cuts and his stance in the Cold War.

bio|06-05|2012|Ρέι Μπράντμπερι|Ray Bradbury|Ray Bradbury was an American writer. He wrote the novel "Fahrenheit 451" and "The Martian Chronicles", and became one of the leading science fiction writers.

bio|06-06|1606|Πιερ Κορνέιγ|Pierre Corneille|Pierre Corneille was a French playwright and one of the founders of French tragedy. His play "The Cid" was a great success in 1637 and caused debate about the rules of the theatre.

bio|06-06|1799|Αλεξάντρ Πούσκιν|Alexander Pushkin|Alexander Pushkin was a Russian poet and writer and is regarded as the founder of modern Russian literature. He wrote "Eugene Onegin". He was killed in a duel in 1837.

bio|06-06|1832|Τζέρεμι Μπένθαμ|Jeremy Bentham|Jeremy Bentham died in 1832. He was an English philosopher and jurist and the founder of utilitarianism. According to his will, his body is preserved as an "auto-icon" at University College London.

bio|06-06|1850|Καρλ Φέρντιναντ Μπράουν|Karl Ferdinand Braun|Karl Ferdinand Braun was a German physicist. He developed the cathode-ray tube and in 1909 shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Marconi for his contribution to wireless telegraphy.

bio|06-06|1875|Τόμας Μαν|Thomas Mann|Thomas Mann was a German writer. He wrote the novels "Buddenbrooks", "The Magic Mountain" and "Death in Venice". In 1929 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature, and he lived in exile during the Nazi period.

bio|06-06|1901|Σουκάρνο|Sukarno|Sukarno was an Indonesian politician. He led the struggle for independence from the Netherlands and was the first president of Indonesia, from 1945 to 1967, when he was overthrown by Suharto.

bio|06-06|1946|Γκέρχαρτ Χάουπτμαν|Gerhart Hauptmann|Gerhart Hauptmann was a German playwright and poet. He wrote the play "The Weavers" about the revolt of the weavers. In 1912 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|06-06|1961|Καρλ Γκούσταβ Γιουνγκ|Carl Gustav Jung|Carl Gustav Jung was a Swiss psychiatrist. He founded analytical psychology and introduced concepts such as the "collective unconscious" and "archetypes". He was initially a collaborator of Freud.

bio|06-06|1968|Ρόμπερτ Κένεντι|Robert F. Kennedy|Robert F. Kennedy was an American politician and the brother of President John Kennedy. He was attorney general and a senator. He was shot and killed in Los Angeles in June 1968 during his election campaign.
bio|06-07|1848|Πολ Γκογκέν|Paul Gauguin|Paul Gauguin was a French painter of post-Impressionism and Symbolism. He lived in Tahiti, where he painted exotic works in vivid colours. He died in 1903.

bio|06-07|1862|Φίλιπ Λέναρντ|Philipp Lenard|Philipp Lenard was born in Hungary and was a physicist. He studied cathode rays and in 1905 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. Later he supported Nazism and "German physics".

bio|06-07|1942|Μουαμάρ αλ Καντάφι|Muammar Gaddafi|Muammar Gaddafi was a Libyan soldier and politician. He came to power in a coup in 1969 and ruled Libya for 42 years. He was killed in 2011 during the uprising that overthrew him.
bio|06-07|1952|Ορχάν Παμούκ|Orhan Pamuk|Orhan Pamuk is a Turkish writer. He wrote the novels "My Name Is Red" and "The Museum of Innocence". In 2006 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|06-07|1954|Άλαν Τιούρινγκ|Alan Turing|Alan Turing was a British mathematician and pioneer of computer science. He formulated the concept of the Turing machine and contributed to breaking the Enigma code in the Second World War. He was prosecuted for his homosexuality and died in 1954.
bio|06-07|1958|Prince|Prince|Prince was born in Minneapolis. He was a singer, guitarist and producer. He became known with the album "Purple Rain" and with hits such as "Kiss" and "When Doves Cry".
bio|06-07|1970|Έντουαρντ Μόργκαν Φόρστερ|E. M. Forster|E. M. Forster was an English writer. He wrote the novels "A Room with a View", "Howards End" and "A Passage to India".

bio|06-07|1980|Χένρυ Μίλλερ|Henry Miller|Henry Miller was an American writer. He wrote "Tropic of Cancer" and "Tropic of Capricorn", which were banned for years because of their sexual frankness. He lived in Paris and Greece and wrote "The Colossus of Maroussi".
bio|06-07|2015|Κρίστοφερ Λι|Christopher Lee|Christopher Lee died in 2015. He was an English actor, known as Dracula in the Hammer films and as Saruman in "The Lord of the Rings".
bio|06-08|632|Μωάμεθ|Muhammad|Muhammad died in 632 in Medina. He was the prophet and founder of Islam, and by the time of his death he had united much of Arabia under the new religion.

bio|06-08|1625|Τζοβάνι Κασίνι|Giovanni Cassini|Giovanni Cassini was an Italian-French astronomer. He discovered four moons of Saturn and the gap in its rings that bears his name. He was director of the Paris Observatory.

bio|06-08|1809|Τόμας Πέιν|Thomas Paine|Thomas Paine died in 1809 in New York. He was an English writer and philosopher who supported American independence with "Common Sense" and the French Revolution with "The Rights of Man".

bio|06-08|1810|Ρόμπερτ Σούμαν|Robert Schumann|Robert Schumann was a German Romantic composer. He wrote piano works and songs, such as "Scenes from Childhood" and the song cycle. He was married to the pianist Clara Wieck.

bio|06-08|1845|Άντριου Τζάκσον|Andrew Jackson|Andrew Jackson died in 1845. He was the 7th president of the United States, from 1829 to 1837, and a general who became a hero at the Battle of New Orleans.
bio|06-08|1867|Φρανκ Λόιντ Ράιτ|Frank Lloyd Wright|Frank Lloyd Wright was an American architect. He developed "organic architecture" and designed "Fallingwater" and the Guggenheim Museum in New York.

bio|06-08|1876|Γεωργία Σάνδη|George Sand|George Sand, real name Amantine Aurore Lucile Dupin, was a French writer. She wrote novels such as "Little Fadette" and was known for her independent life, with relationships with Chopin and Musset.

bio|06-08|1921|Σουχάρτο|Suharto|Suharto was an Indonesian general and president of Indonesia from 1967 to 1998. His government brought economic development, but it was authoritarian and corrupt. He resigned in 1998 after mass demonstrations.

bio|06-08|1955|Τιμ Μπέρνερς Λι|Tim Berners-Lee|Tim Berners-Lee is a British computer scientist. In 1989, as a researcher at CERN, he invented the World Wide Web and developed the basic protocols HTTP and HTML.
